thread:
maria: quick FYI — started seeing a cluster of schema validation WARNs on tool-calls around 08:13 UTC. non-fatal, but routing policy fell back to smaller model which changed outputs and inflated token billing in the console.
kevin: can you paste an example log?
maria: yep — snippet: ```[2026-03-17T08:13:01Z] request_id=r-3a2 schema.validation=warning path=/response/tools/0/output action=routing-fallback model=redwood-xl fallback_model=redwood-small tokens_charged=420```
ash: hm — so these are not hard rejections, just warnings? is the runtime treating ANY schema mismatch as trigger for fallback?
maria: looks like current rule is severity>=warning -> fallback. that's what caused the domino.
ash: that's aggressive. we intended only error/strict failures to trigger fallback. warnings should surface to telemetry/console and let the app opt-in to fallback.
anjali: agreed. two product asks: 1) change default to not fallback on warnings, 2) surface a per-request "schema_warnings" panel in the Console request inspector.
ryan: also need accounting fix. right now UI attributes tokens to the model that actually served (fallback), which is correct technically, but for customers wanting stable billing for the primary service we should emit a "routing_event" telemetry that records first_model + final_model + tokens_by_model. then billing/console can choose how to display.
kevin: +1 on telemetry event. proposed schema: ```event: schema.validation.outcome tags: [severity, schema_path, action] metadata: {requested_model, selected_model, tokens_requested, tokens_served}``` 
maria: can we add a tiny field `violation_level` that is one of [warning, error, fatal] so SDKs and runtime can make consistent decisions?
ash: yeah, that helps. runtime will map current checks -> violation_level. we should publish stable docs so folks don't rely on internal strings.
anjali: UX note: Console should show a colored pill for warnings (amber) and errors (red). and a small CTA: "Treat warnings as errors for this route" toggle (rollout-able).
ryan: rollout plan: default change (no fallback on warning) behind feature-flag -> canary 5% -> 25% -> global. show a console banner for customers affected.
kevin: implementation checklist: 1) runtime: emit schema.validation.outcome event + violation_level 2) telemetry: add routing_event with token split 3) console: request inspector row + route-level toggle 4) billing: expose opt-in stable_billing attribute for route 5) docs + changelog
maria: thanks. who wants which? i can own runtime event + violation_level mapping.
ash: i'll take console inspector and route toggle (will coordinate with UX).
ryan: i'll own telemetry schema and billing display decision. kevin can pick docs and rollout steps?
kevin: sure — i'll draft rollout playbook and docs.
deploy-bot: config change applied to dev cluster: routing.policy.fallback_on_schema_warnings=false (deploy-id: d-20260317-042) :rocket:
maria: deploy-bot shows dev changed — good for validation. i'll send a small test harness that emits warning cases.
anjali: can we add an audit log entry when a route-level "treat warnings as errors" toggle is flipped? compliance will want that.
nash: yes, will include audit hook in the toggle backend.
kevin: estimated effort: runtime (2d), telemetry + billing (3d), console (3d), docs/playbook (1d). schedule to start Monday.
maria: action items captured in the thread: I'll open a tracking ticket and link PRs. thanks all. :thumbsup:
ryan: one more: add a short lived metric `schema_warning_rate` to alerts so SRE can detect if a customer starts hitting lots of warnings after a model change.
maria: good call. will add to ticket.
kevin: ok — triage meeting tomorrow 10am to assign PR owners. closing here for now.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout trigger set for 2026-03-19T10:00:00Z (org:eng-platform)
